title: Sikhism: beliefs and practices

explain.say: Sikhism began in the Punjab region of South Asia with Guru Nanak, born in 1469. He taught that there is one God, and that all people are equal whatever their religion, caste or gender.

draw.label: Guru Nanak's birthplace, Nankana Sahib, and Amritsar in the Punjab

draw.text: Ik Onkar: there is one God

explain.say: Ten human Gurus led the Sikhs over about two hundred years. The tenth, Guru Gobind Singh, founded the Khalsa in 1699 and named the holy scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, as the Guru forever.
The Guru Granth Sahib holds hymns of the Sikh Gurus, and also of Hindu and Muslim holy men. It is treated with great honour, placed on a raised throne under a canopy.

draw.label: pages in the Guru Granth Sahib

draw.text: Written in the Gurmukhi script, sung as kirtan

explain.say: Sikhs live by three duties: remember God's name, earn an honest living, and share with others. Seva, selfless service, is part of everyday life.
Every gurdwara has a langar, a free kitchen where anyone, of any faith, sits together and shares a simple vegetarian meal. The Golden Temple in Amritsar feeds tens of thousands of people every day.

items: Bow before the Guru Granth Sahib
All sit side by side as equals

explain.say: Initiated Sikhs of the Khalsa wear the five Ks: uncut hair, a steel bracelet, a wooden comb, cotton undershorts and a small sword. Many Sikhs also wear a turban.

items: K | What it is | What it stands for
Kesh | uncut hair | living as God made you
Kara | steel bracelet | one God, no beginning or end
Kirpan | small sword | protecting the weak

faq.a: Langar is the free community kitchen found in every gurdwara. Anyone, of any religion or background, can eat there. People sit together, often on the floor, as equals, and volunteers cook and serve a simple vegetarian meal.
asks: Why do Sikhs give free food?
What is the free kitchen at a gurdwara?

faq.a: Visitors cover their heads and take off their shoes. Inside, the Guru Granth Sahib sits on a raised platform, hymns called kirtan are sung, and people receive karah prashad, a sweet offering. Then everyone can share langar.
asks: What do Sikhs do in the gurdwara?

faq.a: The five Ks are worn by initiated Sikhs: Kesh, uncut hair; Kara, a steel bracelet; Kanga, a wooden comb; Kachera, cotton undershorts; and Kirpan, a small ceremonial sword. Each is a reminder of faith and duty.
Guru Nanak, born in 1469 in what is now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan, was the founder and first Guru of Sikhism. He travelled widely, teaching that there is one God and that all people are equal.
asks: Who was the first Sikh Guru?

faq.q: What is the Guru Granth Sahib?
faq.a: The Guru Granth Sahib is the Sikh holy scripture and is honoured as the living Guru. It contains hymns by Sikh Gurus and by Hindu and Muslim saints, written in the Gurmukhi script, and runs to 1,430 pages.
asks: What is the Sikh holy book?

faq.a: Sikhs believe in one God, the creator, present in everyone. They believe all people are equal, and aim to remember God, work honestly, share with others and serve. They believe in rebirth, and that God's grace brings liberation.
Many Sikhs wear a turban, or dastar, to cover their uncut hair, which they keep as a gift from God. The turban is a sign of faith, dignity and equality. Some Sikh women wear turbans too.
asks: Why do Sikh men not cut their hair?

faq.a: The ten human Gurus led Sikhism from Guru Nanak, born in 1469, to Guru Gobind Singh, who died in 1708. Guru Arjan, the fifth, compiled the scripture, and Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth, named it the eternal Guru.
asks: How many Gurus are there in Sikhism?

faq.a: The Khalsa is the community of initiated Sikhs, founded by Guru Gobind Singh at Vaisakhi in 1699. Members take amrit, a sweet water blessing, wear the five Ks, and promise to live by Sikh teachings and protect others.

The Golden Temple, or Harmandir Sahib, in Amritsar is the holiest gurdwara for Sikhs. It stands in a pool of water, has doors on all four sides to show that everyone is welcome, and serves langar to huge numbers of people daily.

faq.q: What do Singh and Kaur mean?
faq.a: Sikh men often take the name Singh, meaning lion, and women Kaur, often explained as princess. Guru Gobind Singh gave these names so that all Sikhs share one family name, rejecting caste.
Vaisakhi, in April, is a harvest festival and the day Sikhs remember the founding of the Khalsa in 1699. Sikhs visit the gurdwara, join processions with hymns, and share langar.
There are about 25 to 30 million Sikhs, most of them in Punjab in India. There are also large Sikh communities in the United Kingdom, Canada and the United States.
asks: Number of Sikhs in the world?

facts: Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, was born in 1469.
Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa at Vaisakhi in 1699.
The standard Guru Granth Sahib has 1,430 pages, called angs.
Sikhism had ten human Gurus, from Guru Nanak to Guru Gobind Singh.
The Golden Temple in Amritsar is also called Harmandir Sahib.
